messages.subject: Additive dominance model
parts:
Hi,

I would like to know if it is possible to use scanone/scantwo with an explicit a priori additive dominance model for each locus, specifying that the heterozygous are expected to have an intermediary effect between the homozygous. 

I've tried to run a marker regression using linear models with each genotype coded as 0, 1, and 2 (as continuous integers, not as categorical variables) and based on some permutations it seemed to have higher power with my data set. Perhaps because my data (RILs) are not fully inbred and there are still a few (5%) heterozygous sometimes the sample size of this group (heterozygous) is very small.

Best,

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: Additive dominance model
parts:
R/qtl doesn't have any facility for additive or dominance models. And for RIL, it omits and ignores any heterozygous genotypes, so there's just one degree of freedom for the effect at a QTL.

karl
